topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the speaker's background, and defines the core learning objectives regarding cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Concepts in Cancer Etiology and Risk Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer development as a multifactorial process driven by genetic mutations, endogenous cellular stress, environmental exposures, and statistical chance.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents such as viruses and bacteria contribute to cancer development, illustrated by the pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical compounds and ultraviolet radiation induce DNA damage through direct mutation, metabolic activation, or oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, focusing on the role of inflammatory microenvironments, tumor promoters, and host developmental stages.

topics.label: Methods for Evaluating Carcinogenicity and Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate human cancer risk.
